svg.text: Rupture · endoleaks · aorto-enteric fistula · Crawford (TAAA) · DVLA
Classic triad — abdominal / back / flank pain + hypotension / shock + pulsatile expansile mass. Mimics renal colic. ~80% die
Endovascular-first strategy: no 30-day mortality difference (~35%) but better mid-term survival, quality of life, shorter stay & lower cost.
NICE: EVAR benefits most (esp. men > 70, women); open better in men < 70.
AAA erodes directly into bowel; no prior aortic surgery
weeks–years post-op; often with graft infection
Herald (sentinel) GI bleed → catastrophic exsanguination. Ix: CTA + OGD (negative does not exclude). Mx: graft excision + extra-anatomic
(axillo-bifemoral) or in-situ reconstruction + antibiotics. High mortality.
Extent predicts spinal cord ischaemia: II (most extensive) highest, IV lowest. Open repair — CSF drainage, permissive
hypertension, intercostal (Adamkiewicz) reimplantation; or fenestrated / branched EVAR.
IMA sacrifice — left colon; bloody diarrhoea, ↑ lactate
paraplegia — esp. thoracoabdominal; CSF drainage protective
late; herald GI bleed — see above
After successful repair with no further enlargement and no other disqualifying condition.
Ruptured AAA mimics renal colic — never diagnose first-presentation 'renal colic' in an older arteriopath without excluding
Don't over-resuscitate a ruptured AAA: permissive hypotension (SBP ~70–90) until proximal control.
Type I & III endoleaks are high-pressure — treat urgently; Type II (commonest) is watched, treated only if the sac grows.
Any GI bleed with a previous aortic graft is a secondary aorto-enteric fistula until proven otherwise — a herald bleed precedes
Crawford extent II carries the highest paraplegia risk — CSF drainage & intercostal reimplantation are key protective steps.
DVLA: Group 1 stop at 6.5 cm; Group 2 disqualified at 5.5 cm.
IMPROVE trial (BMJ 2014; Eur Heart J 2015; BMJ 2017). NICE NG156. ESVS 2019 AAA clinical practice guidelines.
Crawford / Safi thoracoabdominal classification. DVLA Assessing Fitness to Drive (cardiovascular — aortic aneurysm).
MockFRCS revision aid — verify against current NICE / DVLA guidance and local vascular network protocols.
